leaf.question: Does the official GitHub repository-contents API specification establish the r252 premise that concurrent same-path create-without-SHA attempts are linearized so at most one create effect can commit?

source.title: REST API endpoints for repository contents — Create or update file contents

documented_observations: The endpoint is documented as creating a new file or replacing an existing file.
The request body requires `sha` when updating an existing file.
The documented response set includes 409 Conflict and 422 Validation failed/spam responses.
The documentation explicitly warns that using this endpoint and Delete a file in parallel will conflict and must be serialized.
leaf.missing_guarantee: The audited official page does not state that two concurrent create-without-SHA requests against the same absent path are linearizable, does not define a same-key create-if-absent atomicity guarantee, and does not state that exactly one of such concurrent creates must succeed.
leaf.scope: Documentation audit only for GitHub REST repository contents Create or update file contents. No concurrent mutation experiment was performed and no claim is made about undocumented implementation behavior.
leaf.semantic_conclusion: The r252 serialized two-actor proof remains conditionally valid, but the provider-linearizability premise required to extend it to true simultaneous same-path transport is still unresolved. The GitHub Contents API documentation audited here is insufficient positive evidence for that premise.
